action: Citizen submits mutation application with registered deed/succession papers at the Tehsil counter
on_reject: Application not accepted if documents incomplete; resubmit with corrections
note: Report of transfer is made to the Tehsildar under s.34

action: Registers/diarises the application, assigns a case number and issues a dated receipt
note: Diarising starts the statutory clock for disposal

action: Opens the mutation file, verifies fee, and routes it to the field revenue staff
note: File prepared for field enquiry

action: Conducts field enquiry, checks khatauni/khasra entries and possession, files field report
on_reject: Adverse field report may lead to rejection or conversion to contested case
note: first person a citizen meets for any land matter

action: Verifies and countersigns the Lekhpal's field report and khatauni check for correctness
on_reject: Report returned to Lekhpal for correction
note: Kanungo supervisory layer over the Lekhpal

action: Reviews field verification, ensures record consistency, forwards case to the Tehsil court
note: supervisory layer over the field staff

action: Issues proclamation (public notice) inviting objections from interested parties
note: s.35 proclamation; objections define uncontested vs contested branch

action: Lists the case for hearing before the Tehsildar/Naib Tehsildar after the objection period lapses
note: Reader manages the revenue court cause-list

action: Hears uncontested cases and passes the mutation order directing khatauni amendment
time_limit: target disposal within 45 days of application
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Officer (SDM) within 30 days of the order
note: s.35(1) uncontested branch: NT directs amendment

action: For contested cases, adjudicates the dispute after hearing parties and passes the mutation order
on_reject: Appeal to SDM within 30 days; further to Collector/Commissioner
note: s.35(1) contested branch decided by Tehsildar; may take longer

action: Gives effect to the order by amending the khatauni (record of rights) entry
note: Record update executed at village level

action: Updates and preserves the amended record of rights in the tehsil record room
note: maintains the authoritative record copy

action: Issues a certified copy of the updated khatauni to the applicant
note: Certified copy is proof of mutation

action: Citizen applies via e-District/CSC or Tehsil counter; application captured with documents
on_reject: Incomplete applications returned for correction
note: e-District UP is the official channel

action: Generates the acknowledgement number and dated receipt, starting the service clock
note: Acknowledgement triggers the Janhit Guarantee time limit

action: Conducts field verification of residence/caste/income at the declared address and files report
on_reject: Negative verification can lead to rejection
note: Lekhpal checks khatauni, voter list, neighbours

action: Cross-checks and endorses the Lekhpal's verification report
on_reject: Report returned for re-verification
note: supervisory endorsement of field report

action: Verifies the report against records and forwards the file to the signing authority
note: record-check layer

action: Places the verified file before the Tehsildar/SDM for signature
note: Reader manages the signing queue

action: Reviews and digitally signs the caste/income/domicile certificate (SDM where designated)
time_limit: within the Janhit Guarantee statutory limit (~7-15 working days total)
on_reject: Appeal to First Appellate Officer within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
note: designated officer under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011

action: Delivers the digitally-signed certificate via e-District download / CSC to the applicant
note: Certificate verifiable online by certificate number

action: Publishes RTE round notification and readies the state RTE portal, block school list and seat matrix
note: admission is only into entry class (Class 1 / pre-primary) per s.12(1)(c)

action: Parent applies online on the state RTE portal, uploading eligibility documents and choosing neighbourhood schools
note: citizen-facing step; submission is by the parent online

action: Receives application plus documents and verifies eligibility (age, EWS/DG income/caste, residence, distance)
on_reject: reapply in next round or appeal to Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA)
note: neighbourhood: within 1 km (primary) / 3 km (upper primary)

action: Confirms the verified applicant pool for the block/district and forwards the eligible list into the lottery
on_reject: grievance to BSA / District Education Officer
note: only BEO-verified applications enter the draw

action: Oversees the online lottery/random allotment of verified children to specific schools per seat availability
on_reject: waitlist / subsequent round; appeal to CEO/BSA
note: lottery is the decisive allotment event under the 25% quota

action: Signs/issues the official allotment order directing the private school to admit the allotted child
on_reject: school refusal escalated to BSA/CEO
note: binding order under s.12(1)(c); school cannot charge fees

action: Parent reports to the allotted school within the deadline for final document verification
time_limit: within the reporting window on the allotment order
on_reject: non-reporting forfeits the seat; complaint to BEO/BSA
note: reporting step is by the parent at the allotted private school

action: Allotted private school admits the child free of charge and records enrolment against the RTE seat
on_reject: school denial appealable to BSA / District Education Officer
note: actual admitting authority is the private school head

action: Confirms admission, records the child for state reimbursement, and closes the grievance channel
on_reject: appeal escalates BEO -> BSA -> District Education Officer
note: state reimburses per-child cost to the school under s.12(2)

action: Household submits registration application for a job card at the Gram Panchayat with ID/photos
note: registration is free; no fee may be charged

action: Verifies household details, residence and adult members claiming registration
on_reject: complaint to Gram Panchayat / Block Development Officer
note: verification done in the village for transparency

action: Gram Panchayat approves registration and orders issue of the job card to the household
on_reject: appeal to Programme Officer / Block Development Officer
note: job card issued in presence of local residents

action: Issues the physical/e-job card with photo to the household
note: job card valid 5 years; entitles up to 100 days work/year

action: Receives the worker's dated written work application and issues a dated acknowledgement receipt
on_reject: can also apply to the Programme Officer at block if the GP refuses the receipt
note: dated receipt is the legal trigger for the 15-day guarantee under s.3

action: Prepares/selects a work estimate from the shelf of projects to be opened for the demanded labour
note: work drawn from the approved GP shelf of projects

action: Sanctions the work and directs allotment of employment to the applicant household
time_limit: work must be allotted within 15 days of application
on_reject: failure triggers unemployment allowance under s.3(1); grievance to Programme Officer/Ombudsperson
note: the 15-day guarantee is the core statutory entitlement

action: Opens the muster roll and records daily attendance of workers at the worksite
on_reject: discrepancy raised at social audit / to Programme Officer
note: attendance read out to workers at day's end for transparency

action: Measures completed work in the Measurement Book to determine task-rate wages
on_reject: remeasurement / grievance to Programme Officer
note: wages proportional to JE measurement against task norms

action: Checks measurement, prepares the wage/muster-roll bill and forwards the Fund Transfer Order for payment
note: electronic FTO routes wages to worker accounts

action: Authorises wage payment; wages credited to workers' accounts
on_reject: delay compensation at 0.05% per day of unpaid wage under s.3(3)
note: delay beyond 15 days triggers automatic compensation

action: Gram Sabha conducts social audit of works, muster rolls and payments
on_reject: findings referred to Ombudsperson / Programme Officer for redress
note: social audit is the primary statutory accountability route

action: Receives the citizen's building plan and documents online/at counter, generates acknowledgement receipt
note: OBPAS single-window intake; registration of application

action: Checks completeness of documents and fee, forwards the file to the technical branch
on_reject: deficiency memo to applicant for resubmission
note: preliminary completeness check

action: Conducts site inspection, measures plot, verifies setbacks and ground reality against the plan
on_reject: adverse site report returns file for correction
note: field measurement and site-report to higher engineers

action: Technical scrutiny of the plan against bye-laws, FAR, coverage, setbacks; endorses the JE report
on_reject: raises query/objection to applicant via OBPAS
note: AutoDCR auto-scrutiny supplemented by AE bye-law check

action: Reviews AE scrutiny, confirms structural/FAR compliance, recommends the file upward
on_reject: returns file with objections
note: engineering-side recommendation before planning vetting

post_name: Building / Town Planning Officer (Nagar Niyojan Adhikari)
action: Vets the plan for zoning, land-use, master-plan and planning-norm conformity
on_reject: planning objection returned to applicant
note: town-planning vetting

action: Final technical clearance for large/high-value projects exceeding delegated limits
on_reject: returns with technical objection
note: only for cases above lower officers' delegated FAR/area limit

action: Sanctions plans within the delegated financial/area limit on the Commissioner's behalf
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons
note: delegated sanctioning authority for routine/mid-size plans

action: Grants final sanction for plans beyond the delegated limit; approves the permit
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal within 30 days
note: head sanctioning authority (or Vice-Chairman in a development authority)

action: Issues the stamped sanction letter / permit and sanctioned drawings via OBPAS
on_reject: deemed-approval if not communicated within statutory time; appeal within 30 days of rejection
note: deemed-approval provision under Ease of Doing Business

action: Citizen submits application and documents; clerk registers and issues acknowledgement receipt
note: intake at Supply Office / e-district / CSC counter

action: Checks form completeness and documents, forwards the file to the Supply Inspector of the area
on_reject: returns incomplete form for correction
note: preliminary document check and routing

action: Conducts field/home verification of the family, residence and eligibility details
on_reject: adverse verification report can lead to rejection
note: primary NFSA field verification; visits the applicant's home

action: Verifies residence/income/land records in rural areas, corroborates the SI report
on_reject: discrepancy noted in report
note: revenue-side field verification (rural cases)

action: Countersigns/validates the revenue verification and income-residence certification
on_reject: returns for re-verification
note: revenue authority attesting eligibility inputs

action: Scrutinises eligibility against NFSA priority-household / AAY exclusion criteria
on_reject: recommends rejection with reasons
note: eligibility scrutiny before forwarding to the sanctioning officer

action: Approves eligible applications at sub-division level within delegated authority
on_reject: rejection recorded with reasons
note: sanctioning authority where power is delegated to SDM/tehsil level

action: Final approval, sanctions the ration card, allots the category and Fair Price Shop
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal to DGRO
note: card-issuing authority sitting in the district collectorate

action: Prints the ration card, seeds Aadhaar, links the FPS, delivers / enables digital download
note: issuance and FPS assignment via URCMS/e-PDS

action: NFSA grievance: the District Grievance Redressal Officer hears appeals on rejection or delay
on_reject: further appeal to the State Food Commission (NFSA s.16)
note: NFSA s.14 grievance channel; DGRO role often held by a district officer

post_name: Medical Officer in Charge (Hospital / Nursing Home)
action: Institution where birth occurred reports the event to the Registrar and gives parents the birth-report/discharge slip.
on_reject: If institution fails to report, the informant (parent/head of household) files the reporting form directly under s.8 RBD Act.
note: Under s.8-10 RBD Act the head of the institution is the informant for institutional births. Post-2023 amendment, the report is filed digitally on the CRS portal.

action: Create account on CRS portal (dc.crsorgi.gov.in) with parents' Aadhaar and file the birth-reporting form.
note: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (in force 01-Oct-2023) made digital registration via CRS mandatory; Aadhaar of parents is captured. For home births the parent is the informant under s.8.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Registrar of Births & Deaths, Nagar Nigam)
action: Receive the reporting form and documents; scrutinise for completeness and attach supporting proofs.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; informant re-submits missing documents.
note: Required documents: hospital birth-report/discharge summary, parents' Aadhaar/ID and address proof, and (some ULBs) marriage proof of parents. Registrar's office is the urban local body (Municipal Corporation).

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Nagar Nigam — designated Health Officer / Chief Medical Officer)
action: Verify the reported particulars against records and enter the event in the birth register.
on_reject: Objection recorded; informant asked to reconcile particulars or produce affidavit.
note: s.7 & s.12 RBD Act: the Registrar for an urban area is the officer designated by the Municipal Corporation (commonly the Health Officer / CMO or a designated corporation official).

action: Register the birth in the statutory register — this is the decisive registration act.
on_reject: If refused, escalate to the District Registrar of Births and Deaths.
note: s.12 RBD Act: on registration the Registrar shall give, free of charge, an extract of the prescribed particulars. Registration within 21 days carries no fee.

action: Generate and issue the QR-verified digital birth certificate to the informant.
on_reject: On non-delivery within the guaranteed period, invoke the State Right-to-Public-Services appeal (First Appellate Authority).
note: s.12/s.17 RBD Act read with 2023 amendment: the digital certificate carries a QR code and is the single proof of date of birth for those born on/after 01-Oct-2023. UP delivery guaranteed under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.

action: For reporting after 21 but within 30 days, register on payment of the prescribed late fee.
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar.
note: s.13(1) RBD Act. UP prescribed late fee at this tier is nominal (approx. Rs 2). This step applies only when the 21-day window was missed.

post_name: District Registrar of Births & Deaths / Additional District Magistrate
action: For reporting after 30 days but within one year, grant written permission to register on late fee plus notarised affidavit.
on_reject: Apply to a First Class / Executive Magistrate for an order (see next step).
note: s.13(2) RBD Act: requires written permission of the prescribed authority, prescribed fee (approx. Rs 5 in UP), and an affidavit before a notary public. Prescribed authority in UP is typically the District Registrar / ADM.

action: For births not registered within one year, pass a magisterial order directing registration on payment of fee.
on_reject: Revision before the District Magistrate; thereafter writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: s.13(3) RBD Act: registration after one year requires an order of a Magistrate of the First Class or Presidency Magistrate; in UP this is routed through the SDM / Executive Magistrate.

post_name: First Appellate Authority (designated officer, UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam)
action: On delay or refusal, hear the citizen's appeal and direct issuance within the guaranteed period.
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority; parallel RTI to the CMO / District Registrar; complaint to State Chief Registrar (Births & Deaths) / Directorate.
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 provides a tiered appeal with penalty on the defaulting designated officer. Grievance also lies to the District/Chief Registrar under the RBD Act.

action: Issue Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4/4A) to the family.
note: RBD Act s.10 + Rules: attending doctor/hospital certifies cause of death on Form 4 (institution) or Form 4A (non-institutional). In Uttarakhand urban areas the CMO is a designated District Registrar for deaths.

action: Report the death and submit the death report (Form 2) within 21 days.
time_limit: 21 days from date of death (RBD Act s.10 + Rules)
note: RBD Act ss.8-9 fix the informant: for a house death, the head of household or nearest relative; for a hospital/institution, the medical officer in charge; for cremation/burial ground, the person in charge.

post_name: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Health Officer / designated ward-zone Registrar)
action: Receive Form 2, medical cause-of-death certificate, and ID/address proofs at counter or e-district portal.
note: In a municipal-corporation area the Registrar function sits in the corporation Health Dept (a designated Registrar/Sub-Registrar). Documents: Form 2, Form 4/4A, proof of identity of deceased (Aaadhaar), informant ID and address proof, cremation/burial receipt. Apply via UP eDistrict (edistrict.up.gov.in) or Uttarakhand eServices / CRS portal.

action: Verify documents against Form 4/4A and informant particulars for completeness.
on_reject: Return application for missing/discrepant documents; informant re-submits.
note: Registrar checks the report against the medical certificate; if reported within 21 days registration is normal and no fee is charged for entry.

post_name: Prescribed Authority (Additional District Registrar / District Registrar)
action: For delay of 30 days to 1 year, grant written permission on affidavit plus prescribed late fee.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 30 days and within 1 year (RBD Act s.13(2))
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar; ultimately magistrate route under s.13(3).
note: RBD Act s.13: 21-30 days = small prescribed late fee only; 30 days-1 year = registered only with written permission of the prescribed authority + affidavit before a notary + prescribed fee. Skip this step if reported within 21 days.

action: For delay beyond 1 year, pass an order authorising registration after verifying correctness.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 1 year (RBD Act s.13(3))
on_reject: Revision/representation to District Magistrate.
note: RBD Act s.13(3): a death not registered within one year is registered only on an order of a Magistrate of the First Class / Executive Magistrate after verifying correctness, on payment of the prescribed fee. Skip if within 1 year.

action: Enter the death in the register and record it on the national CRS portal.
on_reject: Refusal to register is appealable to the District Registrar / Chief Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: This is the operative decision that completes registration. Post-2023 Amendment (in force 1 Oct 2023) registration on the Centre's Civil Registration System (crsorgi.gov.in) is mandatory and data is shared with the Registrar General of India.

action: Issue the death certificate (digital or physical) free of charge to the informant.
time_limit: Within 7 days of completing registration (RBD Act s.17)
note: RBD Act s.17 (as amended 2023): Registrar gives, free of charge and not later than 7 days, a certificate to the person who gave information under s.8/s.9, electronically or otherwise. Additional/duplicate copies carry a small prescribed fee.

action: Issue additional certified copies on request against the prescribed per-copy fee.
time_limit: State RTS schedule where notified (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand RTS)
on_reject: First appeal (see step 11) if copy not delivered within the RTS time limit.
note: Extra copies are searched and issued under RBD Act s.17; digitally certified copies are downloadable from the UP eDistrict / Uttarakhand eServices portal.

action: Process corrections/cancellations of entries on written application with proof.
on_reject: Refusal appealable to District Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: RBD Act s.15 + Rules: clerical/material errors (name, date, spelling) are corrected or cancelled by the Registrar with a margin entry on documentary proof; not by erasing the original entry.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (Additional District Magistrate / designated officer under state RTS)
action: Hear appeal where service is refused or exceeds the RTS time limit; direct delivery.
time_limit: File within 30 days of rejection or expiry of the stipulated time limit (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011, s.5-6)
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority within 60 days.
note: Under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (and the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act), the First Appellate Officer may order the designated officer to deliver within a fixed period; a second appeal lies within 60 days.

post_name: Second Appellate Authority (Commissioner / senior officer under state RTS)
action: Decide second appeal and may impose penalty on the defaulting designated officer.
time_limit: File within 60 days of the first-appeal decision (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011)
on_reject: Parallel remedy: RBD Act s.25 appeal to Chief Registrar; or writ/RTI.
note: The RTS statute empowers the second appellate authority to penalise the designated officer for unjustified delay/refusal, closing the accountability loop.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (self, or via Jan Seva Kendra CSC operator)
action: Register on UDID portal swavlambancard.gov.in; fill personal, disability and address details.
note: Free. In UP the assisted route is the Jan Seva Kendra / CSC or e-District. An enrolment number is issued to track status. Portal is run by DEPwD. Confidence high on portal/route.

action: Upload identity proof, address proof, photograph, and any existing medical/disability records; select district hospital/CMO.
note: Aadhaar, photo, address proof and prior medical records. Applicant selects the designated assessing hospital / CMO office in their district. Grounded in DEPwD UDID application flow.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (UDID cell, District Hospital / CMO office)
action: Receive and scrutinise application on portal; verify documents; assign a medical assessment date.
on_reject: Application returned on portal for correction/resubmission of documents.
note: The application lands with the designated medical authority selected in Step 2. RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 18(1): medical authority verifies information before assessment.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / Specialist (orthopaedic, ophthalmologist, ENT, psychiatrist as per disability)
action: Examine applicant on assigned date; measure impairment and quantify disability percentage per notified guidelines.
note: Assessment per Gazette Notification S.O. 76(E), 04.01.2018. Single specialist for some categories (e.g. locomotor); a full Medical Board for multiple/intellectual/mental disability. Applicant brings originals.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Civil Surgeon)
action: Deliberate on assessment, fix disability category and percentage, and decide eligibility for certification.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt of application (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
on_reject: If found ineligible, reasons conveyed in Form VIII within one month; appeal under RPwD Act s.59 within 90 days of rejection (Rule 18(4)).
note: The decisive step. CMO chairs the district Medical Board. Certificate issues only if the person is a person with a specified disability (benefits generally require >=40%). Confidence high (statutory).

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Medical Superintendent (competent medical authority)
action: Generate the disability certificate in Form V / VI / VII and digitally sign it on the portal.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
note: Form VII for a single disability; Form V/VI for multiple disabilities. Certificate is valid across the country (RPwD Act s.58(3)). Digitally signed by the competent medical authority.

post_name: UDID Cell, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD, Central)
action: Generate the UDID number and card centrally after certificate approval; enable e-card download.
note: UDID card carries a unique ID, disability type and percentage; single nationally-valid credential. E-card downloadable immediately; generated centrally by DEPwD after the CMO approves. Confidence high on structure.

action: Dispatch the physical PVC UDID card to the applicant's address by post; e-card remains downloadable.
time_limit: Physical card typically 30-60 days (administrative, not statutory)
note: The downloadable e-card is the operative credential; the PVC card follows by post. Turnaround for the physical card is administrative, not a statutory day-count. Confidence high on route, medium on exact turnaround.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (via portal track-status or Jan Seva Kendra)
action: Track status by enrolment number; if stalled beyond one month, escalate to the CMO / designated hospital.
note: Rule 18(3) fixes one month for issuance; delay beyond it is escalable to the CMO/Medical Superintendent, then the portal grievance channel. Confidence high on the one-month peg.

post_name: Appellate Authority designated by State Government (Directorate of Medical & Health Services / State Medical Board)
action: Hear appeal against rejection or wrongly-assessed percentage; re-decide the certification.
time_limit: Appeal within 90 days of rejection (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(4) read with Act s.59)
on_reject: Further complaint of denial of rights lies with the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (RPwD Act, ss.79-80); UP: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in.
note: Section 59 vests appeal in a State-designated appellate authority; the 90-day window is fixed by Rule 18(4). Exact appellate body name varies by state notification (UP: State Medical Board / DGMH). Confidence high on provision, medium on exact body.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (statutory)
action: Hear complaints of deprivation of rights or non-implementation; direct remedial action on the certificate/benefits.
on_reject: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities at the Centre (RPwD Act, ss.74-75).
note: Statutory grievance forum under RPwD Act ss.79-80 for denial of rights (distinct from the medical-percentage appeal). UP court: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in. Confidence high (statutory).

action: Identify area DISCOM and apply online via Jhatpat portal (upenergy.in) declaring sanctioned load in kW.
note: In UP the licensee is a UPPCL DISCOM for the applicant's zone (PVVNL Meerut, MVVNL Lucknow, PuVVNL Varanasi, DVVNL Agra, KESCO Kanpur) or a private licensee (NPCL/Torrent); in Uttarakhand it is UPCL. Application also accepted at Jan Suvidha / e-Suvidha centres or the sub-division office. Domestic (DS) load selectable 1 kW to 500 kW.

action: Upload ID proof, ownership/occupancy proof, photograph; pay application fee (Rs 100 APL / Rs 10 BPL).
note: Ownership proof per Supply Code: registered sale deed / partition deed / succession or heir (vasiyat) certificate; occupant may use rent agreement + owner NOC. Fee amounts are the Jhatpat scheme rates; the refundable security deposit and line/service charges come later via the demand note, not at application.

action: Register application, verify documents for completeness, generate application/registration number.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant re-submits missing documents; deemed-registration on completeness.
note: Scrutiny/registration at the DISCOM sub-division (Vidyut Vitran Khand) serving the address. Incomplete applications are returned with a checklist rather than rejected outright.

action: Conduct site/feasibility inspection: confirm load, nearest distribution pole/point, and technical feasibility.
on_reject: Infeasibility recorded with reasons; applicant may contest via CGRF (step 10).
note: Applicant suggests up to three preferred inspection dates on the portal. The DISCOM JE (Avar Abhiyanta) is the field officer; assesses whether existing mains suffice or a line extension/transformer augmentation is needed - this determines the release timeline.

post_name: Sub-Divisional Officer / Assistant Engineer (SDO/AE, Upkhand Adhikari)
action: Prepare cost estimate and issue the demand note specifying charges and security deposit.
on_reject: Dispute estimate before Executive Engineer or CGRF; excess/erroneous charges refundable.
note: Demand note (Supply Code cl. 4.x) itemizes processing/registration fee, refundable security deposit, and any service-line / system-loading (development) charges. The statutory release clock in step 8 runs from the applicant's compliance with this demand note.

action: Pay demand-note charges and security deposit online or at the sub-division cash counter.
note: Payment (compliance of the demand note) is the trigger event for the statutory release timeline in step 8.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: Sanction the connection and authorize meter installation at the approved load.
on_reject: Appeal refusal/improper conditions to CGRF, then Electricity Ombudsman.
note: This is the decisional approval: the Executive Engineer (or delegated SDO for small DS loads) sanctions supply under the DISCOM's duty to supply (Electricity Act s.43). Sanctioning authority varies with load slab per DISCOM delegation.

action: Install meter and energize the connection within the regulated release period.
time_limit: 7 days (DS, no mains extension) / 15 days (minor extension) from demand-note compliance; longer where new infrastructure needed
on_reject: Delay beyond the standard entitles the applicant to compensation under Standards of Performance / Rights of Consumers Rules 2020; escalate via steps 9-11.
note: UP Electricity Supply Code 2005 cl. 4.15/4.16: supply within 7 days for DS/NRS where no augmentation/erection/extension of distribution mains is required, 15 days where minor extension needed. Uttarakhand (UERC Supply Code) allows up to ~90 days for fresh connections needing infrastructure. Jhatpat scheme markets ~10 days end-to-end.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: First-level grievance: register delay/refusal complaint via 1912 or the sub-division/circle grievance cell.
on_reject: If unresolved, approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (step 10).
note: Internal DISCOM redressal (toll-free 1912 / 1800-180-8752) is the first tier before the statutory forum. Not a separate statute; part of the DISCOM's consumer-service obligations.

action: Adjudicate the grievance if internal redressal fails or times out.
time_limit: Resolution generally within the period set by CGRF Regulations 2022; ~90 days outer limit
on_reject: Approach the Electricity Ombudsman (Vidyut Lokpal) within 30 days of the CGRF order or expiry of the resolution period.
note: Constituted under UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2022 (notified 21-07-2022), at circle and company level. In Uttarakhand the equivalent CGRF operates under UERC regulations.

action: Final statutory appeal: hear representation against the CGRF order or unresolved grievance.
time_limit: File within 30 days of CGRF order or expiry of its resolution period
on_reject: Order binding on the licensee; further recourse only via writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: Electricity Ombudsman appointed by UPERC under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(6) and the 2022 Regulations. Delay compensation under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 / Standards of Performance may also be claimed here.

action: Send intimation of the registered transfer to the Tehsildar to initiate mutation of the record of rights.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §34: on registration of a document creating/extinguishing title to land, the registering authority must send intimation to the Tehsildar in whose jurisdiction the land lies — the statutory bridge from registration to mutation.

post_name: Station House Officer (SHO), jurisdictional police station
action: Give oral/written account; officer must reduce it to writing, read back, obtain signature, register FIR
on_reject: If refused, escalate under s.173(4) to the Superintendent of Police (step 4)
note: For a cognizable offence, registration is mandatory under s.173(1) BNSS — no discretion; Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1 makes registration compulsory. Give jurisdiction over the place of offence, but s.173(1) applies 'irrespective of the area' (zero-FIR): any station must register and transfer later.

action: Issue the free copy of the registered FIR to the complainant immediately
on_reject: Demand the copy in writing; non-issue is itself grounds for the s.173(4) SP complaint
note: s.173(1) BNSS entitles the informant to a copy of the FIR free of cost, forthwith.

post_name: Deputy Superintendent of Police (permission) / Station House Officer (enquiry)
action: Where FIR not immediately registered, verify whether a 14-day preliminary enquiry lawfully applies before deciding registration
on_reject: If enquiry not concluded or wrongly invoked, escalate to SP under s.173(4)
note: s.173(3) BNSS permits a preliminary enquiry ONLY for offences punishable 3-7 years, with prior permission of a DSP-level officer, capped at 14 days. It is not a general escape from mandatory registration. NOTE: for a purely non-cognizable offence, s.174 BNSS applies instead — police only enter it in a register and cannot investigate without magistrate order; the refusal-to-register FIR framing is specific to cognizable offences.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) — or Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in a Police Commissionerate
action: Send substance of the information in writing by (registered) post; SP must investigate or direct a subordinate
on_reject: If SP remedy yields no result, apply to the Judicial Magistrate under s.175(3) (step 6)
note: s.173(4) BNSS: a person aggrieved by the SHO's refusal sends the substance in writing, by post, to the SP; if satisfied a cognizable offence is disclosed the SP shall investigate or direct a subordinate who then has SHO powers. Registered post gives proof of submission. Recourse to the SP is now a MANDATORY precondition before the magistrate route.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (DIG range) then Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG), U.P. Police — Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam
action: Optionally lodge a service-guarantee appeal for non-action within the stipulated time
time_limit: First appeal within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
on_reject: Second appeal to Zonal ADG; independent of, and parallel to, the s.175(3) magistrate route
note: U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 gives time-bound service delivery with a First Appeal (30 days) and Second Appeal (60 days). UP Police designate the First Appellate Officer (DIG) and Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG) for police-service grievances; useful for non-action/delay but does not itself compel FIR registration — the statutory compulsion route is s.175(3).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC), jurisdictional court
action: File an affidavit-supported application asking the Magistrate to direct police to register and investigate
on_reject: If the Magistrate declines, pursue a private complaint under s.223 (step 8) or revision/High Court under Article 226/482
note: s.175(3) BNSS: the Magistrate empowered under s.210 may, after considering the affidavit under s.173(4) and the police's submission on their refusal, order investigation. Attach the SHO complaint, the SP (s.173(4)) complaint and proof of both (Priyanka Srivastava v. State of U.P. (2015) requires the supporting affidavit). Exhausting the SP remedy is a precondition.

action: Consider the application and police submission and decide whether to order FIR registration and investigation
on_reject: Criminal revision, or writ under Article 226 / s.528 BNSS (High Court inherent power)
note: This is the decisive step of the escalation: under s.175(3) the Magistrate must now also weigh the police's explanation for refusal before directing investigation. An order here compels the station to register the FIR and investigate.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) — private complaint bench
action: As an alternative, file a private complaint; Magistrate examines complainant on oath and may take cognizance directly
on_reject: Dismissal is appealable/revisable; can be pursued alongside the s.175(3) route
note: s.223 BNSS (successor to s.200 CrPC): the Magistrate examines the complainant and witnesses on oath and may take cognizance directly, bypassing the police entirely. New proviso to s.223(1): the proposed accused must be given an opportunity of being heard before cognizance. Distinct from the s.175(3) direct-to-police route.

post_name: Director General of Police (DGP) office / UP Police online grievance portal (UPCOP / e-FIR cell)
action: In parallel, lodge an online/e-FIR or written grievance for eligible offence types
on_reject: Portal non-action feeds the Janhit Guarantee appeal (step 5) and the SP complaint (step 4)
note: s.173(1) BNSS recognises information by electronic communication, valid once signed within 3 days. UP Police run online reporting (UPCOP/e-FIR) but scope is generally limited offence types (e.g. vehicle/property theft, cyber crime), not all serious bodily offences — verify offence-eligibility on uppolice.gov.in. A parallel channel, not a substitute for the s.173(4)/s.175(3) chain.

action: Where refusal involves a rights violation or police misconduct, file a separate complaint of police inaction
on_reject: Independent forum; does not compel FIR registration but records misconduct
note: A real but adjunct route for police inaction implicating rights; it addresses misconduct rather than compelling registration, which remains the function of s.175(3). Use alongside, not instead of, the core chain.

action: Confirm eligibility: age 60+, state resident, income below ceiling / BPL, not drawing another pension.
note: UP SSPY income ceiling: Rs 46,080/yr rural, Rs 56,460/yr urban. Uttarakhand: income up to Rs 4,000/month from all sources or BPL. Age threshold is firmly 60+ (draft's 65 is incorrect for the state scheme). 'No regular income' qualifies but must be evidenced by an income certificate or BPL card.

action: Assemble documents: age proof, residence/domicile, income certificate or BPL, Aadhaar, bank passbook, photo.
note: Bank account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT. In Uttarakhand a family register (rural, issued by VPDO) or ration card (urban) is required. Income certificate is itself an e-district/RTPS service if not already held.

action: Issue income certificate through e-District if applicant lacks one; establishes the below-ceiling income fact.
on_reject: Re-apply with supporting income evidence; income-certificate refusal is itself appealable under the state RTPS/Janhit Guarantee schedule.
note: Prerequisite, not part of the pension sanction chain. The income certificate is the key gating document confirming 'no regular income'. Handled by the Tehsil revenue chain (Lekhpal -> Tehsildar/SDM).

action: Submit online application on state Integrated Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in / ssp.uk.gov.in) or via CSC.
note: Corrects draft: intake is the online state portal (or Common Service Centre / Apuni Sarkar e-services in Uttarakhand), NOT the Collectorate counter or the Gram Panchayat form. Applicant selects 'Old Age Pension' -> 'Apply Online', fills personal/bank/income fields, uploads documents, submits. UMANG and myScheme also route here.

action: Field-verify residence and income at village level; in Uttarakhand list is placed before open Gram Sabha.
on_reject: Discrepancy returned to applicant for correction/resubmission before higher forwarding.
note: Uttarakhand rural chain: Gram Panchayat Development Officer (VPDO) -> Assistant Social Welfare Officer recommend; beneficiaries are selected in an open Gram Sabha meeting. This is the local-verification layer the draft was unsure about.

action: Verify rural applications via official login and forward recommended cases to the sanctioning officer.
on_reject: Returned to lower level / applicant if particulars fail verification.
note: On SSPY, the BDO verifies rural applications with a login ID and forwards to the District Social Welfare Officer. In Uttarakhand the BDO recommends onward to the DSWO.

action: Verify urban applications (SDM / Sub-District Officer login) and forward recommended cases for sanction.
on_reject: Returned for correction if urban residence/income particulars fail verification.
note: SSPY urban verification is done by SDM / SDO (in Uttarakhand, Assistant Social Welfare Officer + Sub-District Magistrate). Parallel to step 6 depending on rural vs urban applicant; only one of steps 5-7's paths applies.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Scrutinise the verified case and sanction the pension; approval initiates DBT enrolment.
time_limit: Approx. 30-60 days from complete application (per state RTPS / Janhit Guarantee service window)
on_reject: Applicant may seek review by the District Magistrate / Collector and file a statutory appeal under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act if the time limit lapses or the case is wrongly rejected.
note: This is the actual sanctioning authority, correcting the draft's uncertainty: the District Social Welfare Officer (in UP the District Probation Officer / DPO handles pension sanction) signs, NOT the District Magistrate case-by-case. The DM/Collector is supervisory and appellate. Post-name uses the real official designations.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Release sanctioned pension in quarterly installments via NEFT/DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account.
note: Corrects draft: payment is quarterly (four installments/year) by NEFT/DBT once funds are released by the state directorate (HQ Lucknow in UP), not monthly cash/money order. Nominal monthly rate: UP ~Rs 1,000, Uttarakhand Rs 1,500.

action: Hear appeals against rejection/delay and enforce time-bound delivery under the state Right-to-Service Act.
time_limit: Statutory appeal window under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act
on_reject: Second appeal to the designated appellate authority under the RTPS Act; parallel grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / state social-welfare grievance portal.
note: Escalation ladder, grounded: (1) review by District Social Welfare Officer / DPO; (2) District Magistrate / Collector; (3) statutory RTPS appeal under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam if the service window lapses; (4) CM Helpline / department grievance portal. Confirms the Collectorate's real role here is supervisory/appellate, as the draft suspected.

action: Verify seller's title: pull mother deed, khatauni/record of rights, and Encumbrance Certificate before committing.
note: Record of rights in UP is the khatauni (upbhulekh.gov.in); Lekhpal/Patwari maintains it. EC and chain-of-title confirm the seller can convey clear title. Due-diligence, not a statutory step.

action: Draft the sale deed: parties, property schedule, consideration, and terms; agreement-to-sell optional.
note: Agreement to sell is customary/protective, not mandatory for conveyance. The registrable instrument is the sale deed itself. Confirmed: registration of the transfer is compulsory under Registration Act 1908 §17.

action: Compute and pay stamp duty on higher of consideration or circle rate, plus registration fee.
note: UP stamp duty ~7% of market/circle-rate value (rebates for female buyers; only ₹5,000 for blood-relative transfers). Registration fee 1%, capped at ₹30,000. Paid via igrsup.gov.in e-stamp. Percentages are state-notified rates, subject to change.

action: If consideration ≥ ₹50 lakh, deduct 1% TDS and deposit via Form 26QB before registration.
note: TDS obligation is on the buyer under Income-tax Act 1961 §194-IA for transactions of ₹50 lakh or more. PAN of both parties (or Form 60) is required at registration.

post_name: Buyer via IGRSUP online slot booking
action: Book an online appointment/token at the Sub-Registrar of Assurances for the property's jurisdiction.
note: Registration Act 1908 §23 requires presentation within four months of the deed's execution. UP uses igrsup.gov.in for slot booking. Jurisdiction is the Sub-Registrar covering the property's location.

action: Verify identities of buyer, seller, and two witnesses appearing in person; capture biometrics/photos.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar (Registration Act §72) if refused
note: Registration Act 1908 §34 requires the executants to appear before the registering officer within the presentation window. Aadhaar/PAN, photos and biometrics of parties and two witnesses are taken. The Sub-Registrar (not the District Collector) is the registering authority.

action: Confirm stamp duty/fee paid, admit execution, and register the sale deed in the record.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar / Registrar of the district under Registration Act §72 (except where refusal is on denial of execution)
note: This is the decisive step: registration conveys ownership. Registration Act 1908 §72 gives the appeal against a Sub-Registrar's refusal to the District Registrar. Denial-of-execution refusals go to civil suit under §77 instead.

action: Return the registered original sale deed to the buyer after scanning and indexing.
time_limit: Immediately or within a few days
note: Endorsed/indexed original returned to the buyer. Certified copies remain available from the Sub-Registrar's record thereafter.

action: File a dakhil kharij (namantaran) mutation application with the registered deed and prior khatauni.
note: Registration transfers ownership but not the revenue record; the buyer should still apply for mutation (dakhil kharij / namantaran) online at upbhulekh.gov.in or e-District so the record of rights and property-tax records are updated. Distinct from registration.

action: Conduct field verification, issue public notice, and report on the mutation application to the Tehsildar.
time_limit: Within the Tehsildar's overall mutation timeline
note: The Lekhpal (Patwari) performs the ground-level verification and objection-notice step feeding the Tehsildar's order. An objection window allows interested parties to contest before the order is passed.

action: Decide the mutation and update the khatauni/record of rights into the buyer's name.
time_limit: ~30-45 days (undisputed); specific limit notified under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §3
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Sub-Divisional Officer under UP Revenue Code 2006 §35; then revision to Commissioner under §210. For service delay, first appeal within 30 days under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §6.
note: Tehsildar is the mutation authority under UP Revenue Code 2006 (§34 read with the mutation provisions). This is where the collectorate/revenue side (the stated office class) actually comes in. Undisputed cases run ~30-45 days; contested mutations become a revenue proceeding.

action: If registration refused or mutation delayed/denied, pursue the statutory appeal for that stage.
time_limit: Mutation service appeal within 30 days of rejection/expiry (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6)
on_reject: Registration refusal: District Registrar (Registration Act §72), then civil court. Mutation: SDM (UP Revenue Code §35) → Commissioner revision (§210). Service delay: First Appellate Officer then Second Appellate Authority (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6). Fraud/impersonation: police + civil court.
note: Two separate ladders: the registration-refusal ladder under the Registration Act 1908 and the mutation/revenue ladder under the UP Revenue Code 2006, plus the Janhit Guarantee service-delay ladder. Title/valuation disputes proceed as revenue/civil litigation.

action: Self-check eligibility: UP resident widow, age 18-60, income below rural 46080 / urban 56460 ceiling.
note: Income ceilings ₹46,080 (rural)/₹56,460 (urban) are widely cited; some recent SSPY notifications state a ₹2 lakh ceiling. No remarriage; not drawing another pension.

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Municipality / Gram Panchayat via Panchayat Secretary)
action: Register husband's death and issue the death certificate, the core prerequisite document.
time_limit: Certificate issued within notified days once registration is complete (per Registration of Births & Deaths Act, 1969; state RTS schedule).
on_reject: Appeal to the District Registrar (Births & Deaths); invoke U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam appeal if time limit breached.
note: Death within 21 days is free registration; late registration needs an order. This certificate is mandatory and most confident item.

action: Issue income certificate and domicile/residence certificate, applied through e-District / CSC.
time_limit: Income certificate and domicile certificate are notified services under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (commonly 15 working days).
on_reject: First Appellate Officer (SDM) then Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.
note: Lekhpal conducts the field verification feeding the Tehsildar's certificate. Time limits set by the RTS notification schedule.

action: Register on sspy-up.gov.in, fill the Nirashrit Mahila (widow) pension form, upload documents, submit.
on_reject: Correct and resubmit; contact the DPO helpline 1800-419-0001.
note: Documents: husband's death certificate, Aadhaar, domicile, age proof, income certificate/BPL, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, photo. Print form and submit hard copy to the office within ~1 month.

action: Receive the application, order field verification of widow status, residence and income.
on_reject: Applicant notified; re-verification or correction; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Rural applications route through the BDO, urban through the SDM. Grounded in SSPY process pages.

action: Conduct field/physical verification of widowhood, residence and household income; report back.
on_reject: Adverse report can be contested before the SDM/DPO with documentary proof.
note: Village-level verifier; Gram Panchayat / Ward may endorse. Exact title state-specific but Lekhpal is the UP designation.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / Women Welfare Officer (block-level review)
action: Scrutinise verified application and forward eligible cases to the district sanction committee.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Second-tier scrutiny after field verification, per SSPY four-phase timeline.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / District-level Sanction Committee under the District Magistrate
action: Approve (sanction) the pension and add the beneficiary to the widow-pension roll.
on_reject: Written reasons issued; represent to DPO, then District Magistrate grievance cell; CPGRAMS; RTS appeal where applicable.
note: In UP the widow pension is run by the Women Welfare Dept (Mahila Kalyan Vibhag); the District Probation Officer is the district nodal officer and the sanction committee sits under the DM/Collector.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / Treasury via PFMS
action: Release sanctioned pension by DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account; ₹3,000 quarterly.
time_limit: Fund transfer via PFMS ~1 month after sanction; thereafter quarterly.
on_reject: Report non-credit to the DPO / bank; check status on sspy-up.gov.in with registration ID.
note: ₹1,000/month (₹500 state + ₹500 central), paid quarterly as ₹3,000 by DBT/PFMS. Rescinds if beneficiary remarries or income rises.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) grievance cell / District Magistrate (Collector) grievance cell
action: If delayed or rejected, file grievance; track via portal, DPO helpline, or IGRS/CPGRAMS.
on_reject: Escalate to Director, Women Welfare Directorate; then CPGRAMS; ultimately a writ petition to the Allahabad High Court.
note: SSPY helpline 1800-419-0001; UP IGRS (jansunwai.up.nic.in) and CPGRAMS are the standing grievance channels.

post_name: First / Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011
action: Where the service is RTS-notified, appeal breach of statutory time limit for a directed decision.
time_limit: Appeals decided within the periods fixed by the Adhiniyam (typically 30 days each tier).
on_reject: Second appeal; the appellate authority may impose a penalty (₹250/day up to ₹5,000) on the defaulting designated officer.
note: The RTS route squarely covers the prerequisite certificates (income/domicile) and death registration; whether the pension sanction itself is a notified service varies by the current UP RTS schedule - verify per district notification.
